newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler strike to cut Q2 net by $450 mln.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler strike to cut Q2 net by $450 mln.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. said Monday that the strike at its Mound Road Engine plant and related production losses will reduce its second quarter net income by $450 million, or $0.65 a share, after taxes.
Chrysler said it lost production of 94,000 vehicles during the 30-day strike that ended May 9 and few, if any, of those can be recovered during the remainder of the year.

About 1,800 workers struck at the Mound Road plant in Detroit struck on April 9, forcing Chrysler to halt production at six assembly plants that produce pickup trucks, large vans and Jeep Grand Cherokee sport/utility vehicles.
Chrysler said the strike's pre-tax effect on second-quarter results was $750 million.
Chrysler won the right to move drive shaft production out of the plant, at least temporarily, and agreed to make new investments to bring production of V-6 engine blocks into the plant.

In a statement released Tuesday, United Auto Workers vice president Jack Laskowski said the UAW has a written committment from Chrysler to return the drive shaft work to the plant after the facility is retooled with new production technology.
